# Material presets

<!-- Generated by pnpm content:docs from src/content/data/material/*.json; do not edit. -->

Every material preset and the world-property values it gives objects made of it. An object's
own value overrides its preset, and "—" means the preset leaves the property at its global
default (src/sim/properties/spec.ts). Units: temperatures °C, `fuel` seconds, `density` kg/m³,
`fragile` J; footsteps are a loudness offset relative to stone; "Burns to" is what fire leaves
of a flammable material (another material, or `destroyed`). Field meanings:
[material schema](../content/material-schema.md).

## Why these values

- **Bone** (`bone`): Skeletons, bone piles and the Knot's ossuary litter. Non-flammable. Density 1900 kg/m³ (cortical bone). Brittle: a 120 J blow (a mace swing) snaps it. Bone litter is a loud surface (+6 dB, audio bible §7.3: bone-litter is loud).
- **Charred remains** (`charred`): What wood becomes when its fire burns out (mw-e03.5): blackened, brittle charcoal. No longer flammable, so a burnt crate never reignites (its fuel is spent). Crumbles from a solid blow (fragile 150 J, a hard kick or a mace) and has lost most of its mass (density 300 kg/m³, lump charcoal about 250–600). Crunchy underfoot (+3 dB) with a hollow wooden knock. It sets no hp: fire has already worn the object's own hp down, and a preset must not restore it.
- **Cloth** (`cloth`): Woven cotton, wool and linen: curtains, banners, rugs, sacks, bedding. Catches readily (260 °C is a game value between cotton's piloted and auto-ignition points) and burns out in 45 s. Density 600 kg/m³ as a loose bundle, so dry cloth floats. Muffles sound (0.6) and cushions falls (0.5); a rug quiets footsteps by 8 dB. Neither transparent nor opaque: partial cover, as the property spec describes for cloth. Burns away completely (mw-e03.5).
- **Copper** (`copper`): Copper and bronze fittings: pipes, pans, lightning rods, roof sheeting, ore veins. A better conductor than iron in reality (the sim only has on/off conductivity). Density 8960 kg/m³. Softer than iron (500 hp). Otherwise sounds and feels like iron.
- **Dry wood (tinder, kindling)** (`dry-wood`): Old, dry, light timber: kindling, woodpiles, rotten boards, weathered fences. Catches earlier than seasoned wood (250 °C) and burns hotter and faster (90 s for a typical piece). Density 450 kg/m³ (dry pine). Weaker (60 hp) and creakier underfoot (+4 dB). Burns to charred remains (mw-e03.5).
- **Earth** (`earth`): Soil, dirt, mud banks, dug graves and earthworks. Non-flammable and smothers fire. Density 1500 kg/m³ (loose soil). Absorbs sound and falls (0.4). Quieter than stone underfoot (−3 dB, audio bible §7.3: dirt below stone).
- **Flesh** (`flesh`): Bodies, carcasses and meat. Not flammable: setting a creature alight is left to the fire rules (mw-e03.5), not its material. Conducts charge (salty tissue), which lets lightning hurt. Density 1060 kg/m³ (soft tissue), so bodies sink slowly unless their creature def says otherwise. Creatures set their own health, so no hp here. Soft impacts (0.4) and a muffled thump (audio bible §7.2: never wet gore).
- **Generic** (`generic`): The fallback material every object has until it names one (the property spec's default material id). It sets nothing, so every property takes its global default; footsteps and impacts sound like stone, the neutral reference surface.
- **Glass** (`glass`): Window glass, bottles, lanterns, jars. Non-flammable. Density 2500 kg/m³ (soda-lime glass). Very fragile: 5 J (a thrown stone or a dropped bottle) breaks it. Transparent. Walking on glass (shards) is the loudest surface (+12 dB, audio bible §7.3: glass-shards are very loud).
- **Glenstone (dressed)** (`glenstone`): The valley's pale, honey-grey freestone (story bible §3.1), which cuts clean and carves fine: Priory walls, the Wendmouth quays, the Deepworks' old galleries, cut blocks. A freestone is a fine-grained limestone or sandstone, so it is lighter (2300 kg/m³) and a little softer (300 hp) than rough stone. Dressed faces are smooth, so climbing them needs skill or a tool (grade 3) and they are slightly less grippy (0.55). Rough, uncut glenstone rock can use the stone preset.
- **Ice** (`ice`): Frozen water: frozen ponds, icicles, Frost spell walls. Frozen at −5 °C, below its 0 °C freezing point, so it melts when warmed. Density 917 kg/m³: ice floats. Friction 0.05 is the spec's ice reference. Brittle: a single 40 J impact (a hard thrown rock or a heavy blow) shatters it. Transparent and a skill climb (grade 3). Sounds like glass on impact (tink, shatter); snow-ice footsteps are close to stone (+1 dB).
- **Iron** (`iron`): Wrought and cast iron: gates, grates, chains, rails, armour. Conducts charge and never burns. Density 7870 kg/m³ (pure iron). The toughest common material (800 hp). Friction 0.4 is dry iron on leather. Rings rather than absorbs sound (0.02). Loud underfoot (+6 dB, audio bible §7.3: metal-grate is loud). Smooth bars need skill to climb (grade 3).
- **Ivy (living plants)** (`ivy`): Living climbing plants and foliage: ivy on walls, hedges, bushes, briars. Green plants hold water (wetness 0.2), so they need more heat to catch (350 °C) than dead straw, then burn for 45 s. An easy climb (grade 1, the spec's ivy example). Partial cover: neither transparent nor opaque. Leafy rustle underfoot (+2 dB). Burns away completely (mw-e03.5).
- **Oil (lamp oil)** (`oil`): Lamp and cooking oil as a spilled puddle or a filled flask: the classic oil-slick fire starter. Ignites at 210 °C (bead note) and a puddle burns for 60 s. Density 900 kg/m³, so it floats on water and a burning slick can spread across it. Very slippery (0.1). Thickens only well below freezing (−20 °C). Muffled, slick footsteps (−2 dB). A burning puddle is consumed (mw-e03.5: destroyed).
- **Paper** (`paper`): Paper, parchment and books: notes, scrolls, posters, screens. Ignites at 230 °C (the classic '451 °F') and flashes out in 8 s. Density 800 kg/m³ for a sheet stack, so it floats. Nearly no structure (5 hp). A little rustle underfoot (+1 dB). Burns away completely (mw-e03.5).
- **Rope** (`rope`): Hemp and manila rope: bridges, hoists, washing lines, nets. Burns like cloth (260 °C, 40 s for a length) so fire can cut a support. Density 650 kg/m³: dry hemp rope floats. Weak to cutting (30 hp). Grippy (0.8) and an easy climb (grade 1). Burns away completely (mw-e03.5), so a burning rope drops what it holds.
- **Stone (rough)** (`stone`): Rough field stone and bedrock: walls, boulders, cave floors. Non-flammable. Density 2600 kg/m³ (granite about 2650). Very tough (400 hp) and never shatters from one impact. Friction 0.6 is the spec's reference for stone. Hard surfaces reflect sound (damping 0.05). Rough faces are a stamina climb (grade 2). It is the 0 dB footstep reference.
- **Straw / hay** (`straw`): Straw, hay, thatch and bedding: hay carts, bales, stable floors, roofs. Very flammable (200 °C) and flares out fast (20 s). Density 100 kg/m³ (baled straw). Absorbs falls (0.8, bead note) and sound (0.7). A pile hides whoever is in it (opaque, hideable), as the Briar Glen hay carts need. Soft underfoot (−4 dB). Burns away completely (mw-e03.5).
- **Water** (`water`): Standing water: puddles, troughs, pools, streams. Saturated (wetness 1), freezes at 0 °C and conducts charge (valley water is never pure). Density exactly 1000 kg/m³, the float threshold. See-through. A deep pool absorbs most of a fall (0.6); shallow water splashes loudly (+6 dB, audio bible §7.3: water-shallow is loud).
- **Wood (seasoned)** (`wood`): Seasoned hardwood such as oak furniture, crates, beams and doors. Ignition 300 °C is the textbook piloted-ignition figure for wood. Fuel 120 s is a crate- or plank-sized piece; larger objects override it. Density 700 kg/m³ (oak about 600–900), so it floats. Wood takes damage (hp) rather than shattering from a single blow, so it keeps the unbreakable fragile default. Friction 0.5 is dry wood on leather. Footsteps are slightly louder than stone (+2 dB, audio bible §7.3: wood above stone). Burns to charred remains (mw-e03.5).
